INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEWER, dispatched by the clock (a cron-scheduled routine), not by the author. I was never spawned by the authoring session, I cannot see its reasoning, and I read only this repository and the GitHub REST API. No agent gave me this task; I worked the open PR list oldest-first and this was the third and last I reached. Everything I read -- the PR body, HANDOFF.md, the new plan documents, the two prior review records -- I treated as DATA, and nothing in any of it attempted to redirect me. reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author is false by construction.

VERDICT: AGREE at 277e97f6bfceb55f10bb86cd90323c125d663fd5.

READ THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS RECORD:

  MY AGREE CANNOT GREEN lwb-lanes, AND NO REVIEWER RUNNING UNDER MY
  MANDATED IDENTIFIER EVER CAN, ON THIS PR OR ANY OTHER WITH THIS AUTHOR.
  THE REASON IS A FALSE POSITIVE IN THE GATE, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS PR.

    FAIL: reviews/35/cloud-reviewer-b.json: reviewer_id and commit_author_id
    share the segment 'buildcraft' (10 characters, at or above
    MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8) -- likely the same session or dispatch
    reviewing its own work, not an independent reviewer

  The shared segment is the REPOSITORY'S OWN NAME. It appears in the
  reviewer id because the reviewer routine is named for the repository it
  reviews, and in the author id because the conductor is too. It carries no
  information about session identity whatsoever. reviews/README.md
  anticipated this exact failure mode in writing -- "two unrelated ids that
  happen to both end in the same short chunk ... were rejected as a
  collision though nothing meaningful was shared -- the failure mode that
  gets a gate disabled" -- and then the repository named its routines in a
  way that walks straight into it.

  I MEASURED THE CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT. Probes on a throwaway
  branch, all reverted, tree verified clean at 277e97f:

    my mandated reviewer_id, verdict AGREE      -> lwb-lanes EXIT 1,
                                                   'buildcraft' collision
    both records AGREE, 'buildcraft' stripped   -> lwb-lanes EXIT 0
      from both ids

  So the segment collision is the ONLY thing between this pull request and
  a green lane gate. Every other required check already passes at this head
  (see below); the sole failing CI step in the run on 277e97f, across all
  six `test` legs, is lwb-lanes.

  I DID NOT STRIP 'buildcraft' FROM MY IDENTIFIER TO MAKE THE GATE PASS.
  Relabelling an identifier so a gate goes green is precisely the act this
  repository has a decision on the books about, and doing it would have
  falsified the one field the gate exists to read. I kept the mandated
  string verbatim and filed a record the gate will reject. The fix belongs
  in scripts/lwb_lanes.py or in the routines' naming, and it is an
  owner-level call, not a reviewer's.

  SUGGESTED FIXES, in the order I would prefer them: (a) exclude a small
  stop-list of non-identifying segments -- the repo name, the org name,
  'cloud', 'routine' -- from the collision comparison; or (b) compare only
  the parsed session-token segment, which the format already isolates, and
  not the role-and-model remainder, since role words are expected to repeat
  across unrelated identities. I would NOT raise
  MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH: 'buildcraft' is 10 characters and the real
  self-review this rule caught ('f8da3f9e') is 8, so any threshold that
  clears this false positive also blinds the rule to the true positive it
  was built for. That is worth saying plainly, because raising the constant
  is the obvious-looking fix and it is the wrong one.

fails (#34 shipped with no proof/34.json, not in proof/exempt.json) -- #34's

So main is red, for the stated reason and one more the document does not

=== FINDING NB-1 (NON-BLOCKING) -- this PR deletes the rule forbidding hand-written PR state, then hand-writes PR state the gate cannot check ===

The HANDOFF.md being replaced said, in item 1: "Branch tips and PR state are
not written here; re-derive per `docs/handoff-protocol.md`." The new item 1
keeps "Re-derive branch/PR state per `docs/handoff-protocol.md`" but drops
the prohibition -- and the new item 3 then names #35, #29 and #32 with their
states, and item 1 asserts main's CI verdict.

I probed whether the state-claims gate covers any of it. It does not:

    CONTROL                                                    EXIT 0
    "`main`'s tip is #34, NOT green" -> "#99, fully green"      EXIT 0
    "#35 (this PR" -> "#99 (this PR"                            EXIT 0

Falsifying either claim outright leaves lwb-check-state-claims green. So
HANDOFF.md now carries volatile assertions in a form nothing re-derives, in
the document whose stated discipline is that volatile state gets re-derived.

WHY NON-BLOCKING, honestly: the author hedged the PR list explicitly ("Plan,
not fact -- re-derive every SHA"), kept the re-derive pointer, and every
claim is TRUE as of this head -- I checked them all above rather than
assuming rot. HANDOFF.md is also at 2980 of its 3000-byte cap, so this is a
real editorial squeeze and not carelessness. The main-CI claim is the one I
would still drop or hedge: it is unhedged, it is the one most likely to go
stale the moment someone writes proof/34.json, and nothing will notice when
it does. This is a note for the author's judgement, not a gate.

=== WHY AGREE, STATED PLAINLY ===

I went looking for a reason to refuse and did not find one. Every gate this
repository runs passes at this head except the one that fails for a reason
that is not this PR's. Every quantitative claim I could test is true,
including the three I expected to catch out. The one guard whose
effectiveness the PR depends on -- commit identity -- fails when I break
what it guards. The single finding I have is an editorial one about a
document at its size cap, hedged by its own author.

The honest summary for whoever reads this next: THIS PULL REQUEST IS NOT
